title: SSP-2.2 — Basic Project State Report Evidence
summary: record the ordinary Project State report host, local service and module boundary, live refresh, exact links and basic presentation verification
content_html:
SSP-2.2 — Basic Project State Report Evidence

Outcome

SSP-2.2 is complete at its review gate. The ordinary human-authored Project State document is a normal child of the main dotlineform document and declares viewer_report: project_state with local access. Its generated payload, index-tree placement, Recent entry, and search entry are current.

The Manage report registry and loader now select one focused Project State browser module. The Docs management service owns POST /docs/project-state, runs the accepted SSP-2.1 producer, publishes the matching lookup on normal runs, and returns the complete report and lookup products under one generation. The browser automatically runs on mount, offers Run/Refresh, and renders the Folder, Series, and Docs columns from that response without scanning or joining inputs itself.

Report Behavior

Each Folder cell removes the producer label's leading slash and displays only the first-level folder name while retaining the exact projects/<folder> identity and encoded local-target activation. Series links combine the producer's exact catalogue routes with the configured site-preview base and display only the Series name. Project-document links retain their exact scope, sub-scope, doc_id, and Manage URL. The browser does not display reconciliation-state labels, Series Work counts, incomplete-membership messages, or issue counts; absent Series or Docs values render as blank cells while that evidence remains in the accepted response.

A run disables the pill-shaped 🔄 control, exposes its Run/Refresh accessible name and busy state, updates the status line, and clears the prior rows. A successful response must carry matching report and lookup schema/generation identities before rows render. The completed status starts with the minute-precision GMT generation time and omits a label. An empty response renders a contained no-folders state. A failed request or invalid response retains no prior rows and renders one contained current-run error; the producer's accepted SSP-2.1 failure path retains the prior complete lookup and marks it stale.

Live Evidence

A fresh Docs Viewer service mounted the ordinary host and automatically returned 206 Folder rows, 1,940 matched Works, and 230 Project documents. Explicit Run/Refresh changed the live generated time from 2026-08-05T14:57:55Z to 2026-08-05T14:58:11Z while preserving the same content generation sha256:1f1780659a135713321091b4fd904f62149acc76b61deb851919b1d473b578d0. The persisted lookup is current, has the same generation and 206 folder keys, and records the last refresh at 2026-08-05T14:58:11Z.

The live wa row retains local target projects/wa, links Series 140 as wa, and links its two exact Project documents. The underlying response retains all four reconciliation states plus multi-Series and duplicate-document evidence without changing the three-column row grain.

A post-checkpoint presentation verification rendered the refresh control as a 🔄 pill with the accessible name Run/Refresh, displayed 2026-08-05 15:46 · 206 folders · 1940 Works · 230 Docs, left missing Series and Docs cells blank, omitted the reconciled-row subtitle, and activated Series 001 at http://127.0.0.1:4000/series/?series=001. The 560-pixel report measure retained equal client and scroll widths.

The Series-only refinement was verified against the live 206-row report at 2026-08-05 16:03. The headings were Folder, Series, and Docs; every linked Series label contained only its exact title; 62 absent-Series cells were blank; and no Work-count, incomplete-membership, or issue message appeared in a Series cell.

The folder-label refinement was verified against the live 206-row report at 2026-08-05 16:11. No displayed folder name began with /, no Folder cell contained secondary metadata, and every retained local activation target still began with projects/. The page reported no console errors.

At a 1280 × 800 laptop viewport, the report occupied the existing 560-pixel document measure with equal client and scroll widths for the report, table, and widest row. At 1600 × 1000, the measure expanded to 806 pixels with equal client and scroll widths, including a folder label longer than 30 characters. The first pass exposed a 53-pixel minimum-column overflow at laptop width; the report-specific grid now permits all three columns to wrap within the current content measure. No page console errors remained.

Verification

  • Thirty focused Project State producer, report registry/service, and management-route tests pass together.
  • The Docs Viewer router-module smoke passes for automatic mount, explicit refresh, matching response products, disabled busy state, empty and failure clearing, long linked values, exact folder/Series/document targets, and the POST request shape.
  • Explicit Python compilation, Python lint, JavaScript lint, changed-file sensitive-path scanning, and git diff --check pass.
  • The dotlineform Docs and search builders report four documents, zero warnings, and current generated projections.
  • The public report registry does not expose project_state; the report module and management route retain their local owners.

Independent Review And Stop

The final implementation review found and corrected the laptop-width overflow before acceptance. The subsequent source/diff review confirms that the management adapter only delegates to the accepted producer, the browser requires report/lookup generation agreement, old rows cannot survive a new run or error, folder display does not alter identity, and exact Series and Project-document links come only from the producer response.

SSP-2.3 retained Group by Folder/Series, search, sorting, TSV, and timestamp-prefixed Markdown copy. The completed SSP-2 closeout added no post-commit hooks and transferred consumption-time lookup refresh to SSP-3. SSP-6 retains the older Studio media-audit retirement.
